swipe-to-remove.prompt: can you add a shopping cart section underneath the seasonal favorites on our menu page? list items like Maple Oat Latte, Dark Roast Espresso, and Cold Brew, and implement a swipe-to-remove gesture on each item in the list. please use our team's naming convention: the list should be a ul with class 'SwipeableList', and each item a li with class 'SwipeableList-item' (adding 'is-initialized' once initialized). inside each item, put a 'SwipeableList-track' container and a 'SwipeableList-content' element. when a user swipes past a certain point, the item should show an action color and smoothly collapse down in height to remove it from the page.

checks.message: Track has scroll-snap-type x mandatory
Track has overscroll-behavior-x none
Track hides its scrollbar with scrollbar-width none
Track spacers have scroll-snap-align set to be valid snap targets
Content element has scroll-snap-align set
Content element has an opaque background to hide action behind it
scroll-initial-target nearest is gated behind initialization class
Swipe detector IntersectionObserver is rooted at the track
Swipe detector has low commit and high activate thresholds
Updates data-swipe-direction attribute during swipe
Toggles is-activating class during swipe before commit
Triggers row collapse animation when swiped past commit threshold
Does not drive the swipe with manual pointermove transform updates
MutationObserver wires up dynamically added list items
scroll-initial-target fallback scrolls track programmatically when CSS.supports is false
ResizeObserver is attached to track when fallback is active
ResizeObserver is NOT attached to track when scroll-initial-target is supported
Safari scroll-latching workaround defers item removal and sets inert
Non-Safari browsers remove the item immediately after collapse
Uses WAAPI animations to collapse row height and translate content
Projects focus affordance onto content element when track has focus

scrollability-affordance-hints.prompt: add a customer reviews section below seasonal favorites with a scrollable list of reviews. style the scroll container with a fixed height and vertical overflow, with top and bottom scrollability hints that dynamically show/hide based on whether there's more content to scroll. the top hint should only appear when the user has scrolled down, and the bottom hint should only appear when the user can scroll down further. make sure the hints don't block clicks.

checks.message: The hint at the start edge of the scroller is not visible when the scroller is scrolled to the start.
The hint at the start edge of the scroller is visible when the scroller is scrolled away from the start.
The hint at the end edge of the scroller is visible when there is more content to scroll to.
The hint at the end edge of the scroller is not visible when the scroller is scrolled to the end.
When the content fits in the scroller without scrolling, neither hint is visible.
The hints are drawn with ::before/::after pseudo-elements of the scroller or a mask-image on the scroller, not with extra elements in the markup.
The hints do not intercept clicks on the scrollable content.
Scroll state is detected with CSS scroll-state container queries or scroll-driven animations.
No scroll event listeners are used to show or hide the hints.
When the scroller's scrollbar is hidden and scroll-state container queries are unsupported, the hints still appear and disappear as described above.
When the scroller's scrollbar is hidden and scroll-driven animations are unsupported, the hints still appear and disappear as described above.
When the scroller's scrollbar is hidden and both scroll-driven animations and scroll-state container queries are unsupported, a CSS fallback or an IntersectionObserver-powered fallback is used.

progress-ring.prompt: Update `index.html` on The Daily Grind site to add a loyalty rewards section in the main container alongside Seasonal Favorites, featuring a circular progress ring that visually tracks how close a customer is to their next free drink, displays the current progress details in the center of the ring, and uses styling that matches our coffee shop's existing brand palette.

checks.message: The component contains a native HTML <progress> element
The visual progress ring is implemented using a CSS conic-gradient
The center of the progress ring is transparent or "hollowed out" using background-clip: border-area
When background-clip: border-area is not supported, the center of the ring is hollowed out with a radial gradient mask
The value attribute on <progress> is used to drive the visual progress of the ring using attr()
When using attr() on non-content properties is not supported, a MutationObserver monitors the value attribute and updates the --value custom property
The ring smoothly transitions between values when the --value property is updated (requiring @property support in the browser)
The <progress> element includes an aria-label for accessibility
The component has a distinct visual "track" (background) behind the progress fill
The progress ring respects prefers-reduced-motion by changing to a new value immediately, rather than having a smooth transition
The component is visible on the page
The component supports displaying text content (e.g., the percentage) in the center of the ring

passkey-authentication.prompt: Implement passkey authentication in index.html, ensuring the sign-in username input field with data-testid="username-field" offers registered passkeys as autofill suggestions on focus, clicking the button with data-testid="auth-button" prompts for biometrics directly, request options are fetched from /api/login/options, and authenticated credentials are sent to /api/login/verify to update the element with data-testid="auth-status" on success.

checks.message: The HTML form annotates the username input element with autocomplete="username webauthn"
The client feature detects capabilities using PublicKeyCredential.getClientCapabilities and skips initializing Conditional UI when conditionalGet is not available
The client decodes fetched credential options via parseRequestOptionsFromJSON before invoking navigator.credentials.get
The application registers Conditional UI suggestions automatically on load with mediation="conditional"
The explicit passkey sign-in button click aborts pending Conditional UI autofill suggestions prior to prompting users
If the server verification endpoint returns an explicit HTTP 404 status, PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential is invoked passing the Base64URL credential ID
A successful credential verification updates the UI status to indicate successful authentication and session establishment

menu.prompt: Update the navigation bar and seasonal favorite cards in index.html with an interactive menu component that lets users choose from a list of actions and options, including multi-level nested submenus for drink categories and order customizations. Order customizations include at least one on/off option and at least one pick-one option.

checks.message: Each trigger is a button[type="button"] with aria-haspopup="menu", commandfor, command="toggle-popover", and no popovertarget or popovertargetaction

Each popover is the immediate next sibling of its trigger, submenus are popover="auto" placed after trigger inside parent focusgroup without aria-details, and closed submenus are not inline

Focusing a submenu trigger previews its submenu and sets aria-expanded="true" without moving focus into the submenu, and moving focus to a sibling item closes that submenu and sets aria-expanded="false"
Pressing Enter or Space on a previewed submenu trigger closes that preview and sets aria-expanded="false" without moving focus from the trigger
Pressing Enter or Space on a closed trigger opens its menu, sets aria-expanded="true", and moves focus to the first enabled item
Pressing ArrowDown on a top-level trigger opens its menu if closed and moves focus to the first enabled item, including when opened by pointer and focus is on trigger
Inside an open menu, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move focus between enabled items, and Home and End move focus to first and last enabled item

Pressing ArrowRight on a submenu trigger opens the submenu and moves focus to its first enabled item, while pressing ArrowLeft in a submenu closes only that submenu and restores focus to its parent trigger

Pressing Tab from a trigger or inside an open menu closes all open menus and leaves the menu system instead of stepping through every command

Clicking a closed trigger opens its menu with focus left on the trigger (no item focused), clicking an open trigger closes its menu and leaves focus on the trigger, and clicking outside closes every open menu level
Opening a menu by pointer keeps focus on its trigger with no item focused or matching :focus-visible; opening by keyboard focuses the first enabled item
Any open or close animation is under 150 ms, changes only opacity and a small translate, is off under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, and never delays focus
Moving the pointer over a menu item focuses that item without a visible focus ring, so at most one item is styled as active at a time
Moving the pointer over a submenu trigger previews its submenu after a short delay, and moving to a sibling item closes that submenu
A diagonal move from the middle of a submenu trigger to any item in its submenu keeps the submenu open (a safe triangle), while moving to a sibling item outside that path closes it
Activating a command item closes all open menu levels, restores focus to the root menu trigger, and never leaves focus inside hidden content
A submenu trigger only opens its submenu and never also runs a command; a default action is the first submenu item or a separate command item
Checked items render a visible check mark in the leading slot (::before content is not empty); unchecked items do not
At a 375 px viewport, an open submenu sits directly below its trigger item and its box does not intersect the trigger box
After a pointer activation of a command, focus returns to the root trigger without :focus-visible
